$comment: Per-topic grades for site/quaestiones.json: whether a reader arriving with the topic's own
`question` leaves with it answered by the anchored passages. The METHOD, the scale and every
general finding are in docs/research/topic-anchor-review.md; only the rows live here, so a
grade has one copy.
WHY JSON RATHER THAN THE TABLE IT REPLACED: a grade is a claim about a particular anchor set,
and anchor sets change. `anchors` states the set that was graded, quaestiones.test.ts
recomputes it from the source, and a mismatch is the one defect a markdown table could never
report -- a topic re-anchored after somebody read it, still showing the old verdict. The test
FAILS on drift and names the topic, its graded set and its current one; the fix is to re-read
the topic, not to paste the new signature in. Being made to look is the whole mechanism.
GRADES. A: the passages answer the question as asked, in their own words. B: the answer is
there but the reader has to carry it across from a passage written about an adjacent thing --
a real grade, not a soft A, and the note says what would replace it. C: something the title,
question or keywords promise has no anchored text and the corpus HAS a text -- fix it, do not
file it. D: the missing half needs a document the corpus does not have; see the blocklist in
docs/research/topics.md.
NO C OR D IS RECORDED HERE and that is by design: a C found is a C fixed in the same pass, so
`was` is where they appear. A topic that cannot be fixed is a D and belongs to the blocklist
rather than to this file.
ABSENCE IS NOT A PASS. A topic missing from `reviewed` has not been read. The pass runs a
cluster at a time and the markdown says which are outstanding.

aegritudo.note: CCC 1500–1513 is the Anointing article's own four headings whole, and 1505 and 1508 say the thing the reader needs — _he did not heal all the sick_, and _my grace is sufficient for you_.

finis-vitae.note: 2278 answers "must every treatment be continued" in its first clause and names who decides. Inside `euthanasia`, correctly: this reader is a family at a bedside, not an argument.

post-mortem.note: `lead` 1032 answers the second half of the question, prayer for the dead. can. 1176 added 2026-09-10 for _funeral, wake, burial_; its §2 is written about the living. Keywords reach into grief.

infans-non-baptizatus.note: `lead` 1261 is the whole topic — _allow us to hope that there is a way of salvation_. can. 1183 added 2026-09-10 for the _stillborn_ and _miscarried_ keywords: a funeral can be permitted.

mors-voluntaria.note: See the duplicate note below. can. 1176 and 1184 added 2026-09-10: funerals are owed to the faithful, and the list of those deprived of them does not include suicide.

crematio.note: "May a Catholic be cremated" is 2301; "and may the ashes be scattered" is in _Ad resurgendum cum Christo_, which the page names and does not quote. No quotable work in the corpus answers it.

matrimonium.note: CCC 1626 and can. 1057 both say consent makes the marriage, which is the question's own words. Was short one keyword: _convalidation_ had no text, fixed 2026-09-10 with can. 1156–1160 taken as the chapter. _banns_ still promises nothing.

matrimonium-mixtum.note: CCC 1633–1637 is the Catechism's own heading whole, and can. 1125 answers the second half of the question — _and of which of us_ — by listing promises the Catholic party makes and the other party is only told about.

infidelitas-coniugis.note: `lead` 1649 opens on the Church permitting physical separation, and can. 1152 states the right in law. The keywords reach into `divortium` and `nullitas-matrimonii`; both exist, so the search returns all three rather than the wrong one.

nullitas-matrimonii.note: Was C: "Am I still married?" was answered with venue rules — which tribunal is competent — and never with the grounds, though _defect of consent_ is a keyword. Fixed 2026-09-10 with can. 1095 and 1103.

communio-post-divortium.note: Was C and a strict subset of `nullitas-matrimonii`: two shared paragraphs and nothing of its own. Fixed 2026-09-10 with CCC 1385, the general rule 1650 applies, and can. 915–916, where the reader can see they are not the excommunicated case.

graviditas.note: Was C, and the worst door mismatch found: a page titled _Pregnancy and miscarriage_ whose second paragraph called abortion an abominable crime. 2271 dropped and 1261 added 2026-09-10.

sterilitas.note: `lead` 2379 is "what is left to us" in the Catechism's own words, down to adoption. `fecundatio-artificialis` sits inside it, which is the documented pair.

adoptio.note: can. 110 answers "is the child ours in the Church's eyes" verbatim, and can. 1094 covers the keyword nobody expects to need.

educatio-filiorum.note: Was C: every anchor was the parents' duty to teach, and the question is what to do when the child refuses. 2217 and 2230 added 2026-09-10 — the child at home, and the adult who chooses.

filius-a-fide-lapsus.note: Was C: "Where did we go wrong?" was answered with eleven paragraphs on what parents owe, which reads as the indictment. CCC 1730–1732 added 2026-09-10 — _man is the father of his acts_.

parentes.note: Was C: nothing met _abusive mother_ or _cut them off_. 2232 added 2026-09-10 — _family ties are important but not absolute_ — though its own context is vocation. No paragraph addresses an abusive parent.

cura-parentum.note: "I cannot do it all" is answered by three words inside 2218, _as much as they can_. Nothing in the corpus is about the carer; CSDC 222 is about valuing the elderly. Adjacent to the blocklist.

amissio-operis.note: `lead` 2436 is the Catechism saying unemployment wounds its victim's dignity; CSDC 287 calls it a real social disaster.

pornographia.note: Was C: three paragraphs of definition and nothing on "not being able to stop", while the keywords opened on _addiction_. Fixed 2026-09-10 with 2342 (self-mastery is never acquired once and for all) and 1735.

masturbatio.note: CCC 2352's closing sentence answers "is it always a mortal sin" in the Catechism's own words, and 1735 generalises it.

homosexualitas-vivenda.note: 2358–2359 is a what-do-I-do text rather than a teaching, which is the whole reason it is a separate topic from `homosexualitas`, which keeps 2357.

post-contraceptionem.note: Was C twice over: no anchored text said the word _sterilisation_, and "what now?" was answered only by 2370, which is `contraceptio`'s own teaching restated. Fixed 2026-09-10 with 2399 and 1451–1453.

adulterium.note: "Do I have to tell?" is answered only by 2487, which is written about offences against truth and reputation and reaches a spouse by analogy — correctly, since it says reparation is owed and may be made secretly. Checked: no better paragraph.

remissio-peccatorum.note: Was C: CCC 982 answers "too grave to be forgiven" in its first line, and the keyword _sin against the holy spirit_ had nothing at all. Fixed 2026-09-10 with 1864, which quotes Mt 12:31 and then says what the refusal actually is.

reditus.note: Was C, and a strict subset of `scrupulositas` besides: 1455–1458 is what confession requires, including the annual obligation this reader has not kept. Fixed 2026-09-10 with 1439 (the prodigal son, the journey back, the welcome) and 1465 to close.

scrupulositas.note: Was C by ordering alone: the page opened on 1454, _prepare by an examination of conscience_, which is the one thing this reader cannot stop doing. `lead` 1456 now opens on the answer — _strive to confess all the sins that they can remember_ — 2026-09-10.

post-abortum.note: Was C: 2272 named the excommunication and nothing said it could be lifted. Fixed 2026-09-10 with CCC 1463 and the topic's first canon, 1357, where a confessor may remit it in the internal forum.

venia-danda.note: "Do I have to?" is answered inside 2843 — _it is not in our power not to feel or to forget an offense_ — after that paragraph's own opening on the merciless servant. No ordering surfaces it without splitting a paragraph, which the file forbids.

mortis-desiderium.note: `lead` 2283 puts _we should not despair of the eternal salvation of persons who have taken their own lives_ first, which is the question verbatim, and 2282 closes on diminished responsibility. See the keyword note below.

dubium-fidei.note: Was C: nothing anchored said faith is ever dark. Fixed 2026-09-10 by widening 162 to the Catechism's own 162–165 and adding 2731 on dryness.

amor-dei.note: Was C: 218–221 is God's love for **Israel**, and the reader's whole objection is that it applies to everyone but them. Fixed 2026-09-10 with CCC 604–605 anchored ahead of it, which also retired the `lead`.

oratio-inaudita.note: CCC 2734–2741 is the Catechism's own two headings on this exact question, taken whole and unreordered — the ideal case, where the topic is barely editorial. 2737 lands hard on a reader whose petition was for a dying child; excising it would be choosing by hand.

divinatio.note: 2116 lists horoscopes, palm reading, clairvoyance and mediums by name, which is "what is actually forbidden" answered in the Catechism's own inventory.

signa.note: It gives the posture — trust providence, do not demand proof — and never adjudicates a particular event, which is the honest answer. _Opened the bible at random_ is 2116's.

mortui.note: Nothing says the dead do not return; 1022 added 2026-09-10 so the reader can at least see they are already judged, and 2116 forbids summoning them. The inference is theirs.

daemones.note: Was C by ordering: "Does the Church still do that?" was answered in the seventh paragraph. `lead` 1673 set 2026-09-10.

angeli.note: Was C by ordering: the guardian angel is 336, last of nine. `lead` 336 set 2026-09-10.

apparitiones.note: Two paragraphs, and 67 answers "does a Catholic have to believe" outright. Nothing on how an apparition is approved; the corpus has no text.

miracula-et-reliquiae.note: CCC 1674 is the only paragraph in the Catechism that says "relics", and it says it in a list. 828 added 2026-09-10 for _canonisation_. Nothing on incorrupt bodies.

experientia-mortis-proximae.note: 1021–1022 gives the framework — judgment at the moment of death — and the corpus says nothing about near-death experiences. The reader carries it across or nothing does.

finis-mundi.note: 675–676 is the Antichrist and the rejection of millenarianism, which is exactly what _rapture_ and _three days of darkness_ are owed.

oratio.note: Was C: the Catechism gives three expressions of prayer and the topic carried two, while _contemplation_ and _mental prayer_ were keywords. 2709–2712 added 2026-09-10.

ieiunium.note: can. 1251 and 1252 are the days and the ages, which is the question exactly. can. 919 added 2026-09-10 for the eucharistic fast, a keyword with no text behind it.

dominica.note: 2181 names the grave sin and the excusing reasons in one paragraph, and 2183 covers the case where Mass is impossible.

otium.note: 2185's _the charity of truth seeks holy leisure_ and CSDC 284's _rest from work is a right_ answer a reader who suspects doing nothing is a fault.

initiatio-adultorum.note: 1232 names the RCIA and can. 851 and 865 say what the catechumenate asks. _Baptised as a baby, never confirmed_ is a different path and only 1231 glances at it.

baptismus-infantium.note: can. 874 is the godparent question answered as a checklist, and 1255 says what is asked of them. See the Latin clause noted below.

organorum-donatio.note: 2296 answers both halves of the question in one paragraph, in life and after death, including consent.

corpus-ornandum.note: The Catechism does not contain the word "tattoo" or "piercing"; 2289 gives the principle against the cult of the body. 2290 added 2026-09-10 for _gym_ and _dieting_.

decimae.note: The answer is that there is no number — _each according to his abilities_ — which is what a reader holding the word _tithe_ most needs to be told.

vota-et-iuramenta.note: 2102 defines a vow verbatim and 2103 closes on dispensation, which is the keyword a reader who has broken one arrives with.

vocatio.note: Was C and the clearest case of a title read as an oracle: CCC 1877–1889 says "vocation" and means subsidiarity and socialisation. Replaced 2026-09-10 with 2013–2016, 1533–1535, 898–900 and 2233.

merces-iusta.note: 2434 says what a wage is supposed to cover, at the length of the question, and CSDC 304 covers the strike the title also promises.

pecunia-collocanda.note: Was C: the topic is titled _Investing and speculation_ and the paragraph naming speculation, 2409, was on the tax page. 2409 and 2413 (games of chance) added 2026-09-10.

tributum.note: 2240 makes paying taxes morally obligatory in its first line, which answers "is cheating on it a sin" without needing a second paragraph.

invidia.note: 2539 names the sadness at another's goods and 2540 gives the remedy: _rejoice in your brother's progress_.

acedia.note: 2094 and 2733 both name acedia, and 2733's _a form of depression due to lax ascetical practice_ is the sentence. _Spiritual dryness_ is 2731 and belongs to prayer, which is the distinction worth making.

discrimen-gentium.note: 1935 names race. Was diluted: CSDC 146–147 is male and female complementarity and 148 is disability, neither of which is racism; narrowed to 144–145 on 2026-09-10.

mercatura-hominum.note: 2414 forbids human beings "being bought, sold and exchanged like merchandise", which is the question in the Catechism's own words.

violentia-domestica.note: Was C and the most consequential: one paragraph, about rape, and nothing telling a reader being beaten that they may leave. CCC 1649 and can. 1153–1154 added 2026-09-10.

violentia-digitalis.note: Was C: privacy was anchored at 2488–2492 and reputation, which the title promises, was not. 2477–2479 added 2026-09-10 — detraction and calumny, which is what _gossip_ and _cancelling_ are.

debilitas.note: 2276 uses the title's own word and CSDC 148 develops it. 2274 added 2026-09-10 for _prenatal screening_, which is how most readers arrive at this page.

carceres.note: CSDC 402–404 answers what may be done to an offender, and 405 states the death-penalty teaching as it stood before CCC 2267 was revised in 2018. Both are kept: choosing between two magisterial texts is not this file’s to do. B because the reader is shown the older position with nothing on the page saying when either was written — see the open question in docs/research/topic-anchor-review.md.

defensio-sui.note: 2264 answers "how far" with the moderation test. Was diluted: 2317 and CSDC 500–501 are states at war, which is `bellum`, and were dropped 2026-09-10.

proles-suscipienda.note: CSDC 232 carries the phrase the reader needs — _to avoid for a time or even indeterminately a new birth_ — beside 2368's warning against selfishness.
